section_1.title: The Intuition: Contextual Awareness
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of 'selective focus.' Explain that just as humans focus on specific words to understand a sentence, models must determine which parts of an input are relevant to others.
section_1.example: In the sentence 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired,' the model must link 'it' to 'animal' rather than 'street'.

section_2.title: The Mechanism: Queries, Keys, and Values
section_2.content: Define the Q, K, and V vectors. Explain them via an analogy: Q (Query) is what I am looking for; K (Key) is what information is available; V (Value) is the actual content once a match is found.
section_2.example: Like a library database: You type a search query (Q), the system matches it against book titles (K), and returns the actual page content (V) based on the relevance score.

section_3.title: Visualizing Attention Scores (Dot-Product)
section_3.content: Explain how relevance is calculated using the dot product between Q and K. Introduce the Softmax function as a 'weighting machine' that converts raw scores into percentages that sum to 100%.
section_3.example: Visualized as a heat map matrix: High-relevance words glow bright gold, while irrelevant ones fade to dark blue, creating a 'focus spotlight' on the sentence.

section_4.title: Multi-Head Attention: Seeing the Whole Picture
section_4.content: Explain why one 'spotlight' isn't enough. Multi-head attention allows the model to look at different parts of the data simultaneously—one head might focus on grammar, another on sentiment, another on entities.
section_4.example: Like a team of detectives: Detective A focuses on who did it, Detective B focuses on where it happened, and Detective C focuses on when it happened. Together, they build a complete report.

section_5.title: Synthesis: The Transformer Core
section_5.content: Summarize how these weighted values (V) are combined to form a new, context-aware representation for each word, allowing the model to 'understand' complex relationships.
section_5.example: A final animation showing a jumbled 'bag of words' entering the attention layer and emerging as a structured, meaningful sequence ready for text generation.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
